page: Amazon Web Services i7i.xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 937 GB NVMe SSD. Network connectivity is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2299.0 placing it in the top tier. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression at 34.34 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.1 GB/sec rank in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show relative limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 4390.87 and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression of 28.17 GB/sec fall into the bottom 25%, as does the memory bandwidth read-only large block test at 33.73 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the i7i.xlarge offers a high density of local NVMe SSD storage and DDR5 memory relative to its 4 vCPUs, making it a specialized option for workloads requiring fast local storage access without requiring massive multi-core compute scaling. The instance is suited for database operations, caching layers, and single-threaded data processing tasks, supported by its average Passmark database operations score of 3276.07 and Redis SET throughput of 6.18 million operations per second.
description: Amazon Web Services i7i.xlarge is a storage-optimized server featuring 4 vCPUs and 2 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.2 GHz. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory and a bundled 937 GB local NVMe SSD, operating on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, with its Geekbench single-core score of 2299.0 ranking in the top 10% and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 34.34 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core and memory read bandwidth benchmarks show weaker performance, placing in the bottom 25%. Qualitatively, the server provides a balanced resource profile for storage-heavy workloads that do not require extensive parallel compute scaling. It is suited for database operations, caching, and text processing, supported by a Redis SET throughput of 6.18 million operations per second.
